title: Runtime failure standards and interactive debug graph for inference errors
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: We lack a consistent runtime failure standard across the inference stack, which makes dashboards and oncall investigations slow: engineers see vague 'model error' or 'timeout' labels with no structured reason codes. This work defines a compact failure signature taxonomy, implements tracehook enrichment and a metrics/logs pipeline to emit standardized failure_code tags, and surfaces an interactive debug graph (graph view of request → queueing → gRPC → model kernel) in the Console. Goals: 1) Produce a failure signature spec that covers: client timeouts, edge network errors (HTTP/gRPC 4xx/5xx mapping), queueing/backpressure overload, GPU OOM, KV-cache misses/evictions, model rejections (safety/quality), tokenization/decoding errors, and early termination reasons. 2) Add tracehook enrichers at the request router and runtime entry to attach failure_code and failure_trace with minimal perf overhead. 3) Extend log/metric pipeline (Fluentd -> kafka -> OLAP) to index failure_code and expose rollups per route/model/region. 4) Build an interactive debug graph in Console for SRE/SEs showing causal span chains and the top contributing signals for the failure_code. Success metrics: - Mean time to root cause (MTTR) for P1 inference incidents reduced by 30% within two releases. - At least 90% of terminal errors emitted include one of the standardized failure_code tags. Non-goals: This ticket does not implement auto-remediation or automated rollbacks; those will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Published failure signature spec in Confluence with canonical codes and examples for each runtime layer
Tracehook enrichment implemented for router and runtime with <1% p50 latency increase in synthetic tests
Pipeline indexed failure_code and a queryable OLAP table with daily rollups
Console debug graph MVP that links a sampled trace to related metrics, logs, and the failure_code with clickable span drilldowns
Runbook updated with mapping from failure_code to suggested triage steps and owners

decisions: Use compact dotted failure_code namespace: layer.component.reason (eg: runtime.queue.overload, model.decode.bad_token, transport.grpc.14) to make aggregation straightforward
Emit both failure_code and a human_readable_failure field for backward compatibility with existing dashboards
Sampling: tag all terminal failure events for ingestion but only sample 0.5% of full trace payloads to keep costs bounded
Use existing kafka topic 'infra.errors' to avoid adding many small topics; add schema versioning for the new fields
